output.technical_predicate: On erasure of an eligible abandoned application, the case row and all business-retrievable copies (summary, events, pending jobs) are deleted, while an unrelated active case remains retrievable, and later job replay (drain) cannot recreate or resurrect the erased target.
applicability_facts: Scenario: the abandoned application is no longer necessary; no mandatory retention, prior external disclosure or other exception applies (GDPR Art. 17(1)(a) ground present, Art. 17(3) exceptions absent).
Scenario: an unrelated active case remains necessary and must stay available.
store.py:0210-0212 erase action requires stage=='abandoned' and executes DELETE FROM cases WHERE id=?
store.py:0039-0044 summaries, events and jobs reference cases with ON DELETE CASCADE, and store.py:0026 enables PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON, so dependent copies are removed with the case row.
store.py:0124-0143 drain selects jobs by cid from the jobs table; with the case and its jobs deleted there is no row to replay.
store.py:0055-0058 get_case scopes access to owner/officer, so an unrelated active case is unaffected by deleting another cid.
relevant_exceptions: Art. 17(3) exceptions (retention obligation, legal claim, etc.) are stipulated absent in this fixture; no code path implements a retention override for erase.
Erase is limited to stage=='abandoned' (store.py:0211); non-abandoned cases are out of scope of this obligation.
required_controls: Eligibility gate: erase only when stage=='abandoned' (store.py:0211).
Deletion of the case row (store.py:0212) with foreign-key cascade removing summaries, events and jobs (store.py:0039-0044, 0026).
No residual job rows for the erased cid, so drain (store.py:0124-0143) cannot re-emit events or change stage for the target.
Isolation: unrelated active case remains retrievable via get_case/dashboard (store.py:0055-0058, app.py:0077).
assessment_limits: No execution, database inspection or replay was performed; conclusions are from static source reading only.
Cascade deletion depends on PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON being effective on the connection used for the erase transaction (store.py:0026); not verified at runtime.
Copies outside the modeled tables (e.g., receiver payloads, choices, logs, backups) are not addressed by the erase path and are outside the named predicate's scope.
Compliance is not decided from the rule text alone; only the supplied source coordinates are assessed.
